p.src: Now Baochai had Xiren find out what had happened. Fearing that Baoyu might grieve himself into an illness, she made a show of casually discussing Daiyu's dying words with Xiren, saying, “While people are alive, they have thoughts and feelings; but once they die, each goes their own way, and things cannot remain as they were in life. The living may cherish a foolish devotion, but the dead know nothing of it. Besides, since Miss Lin said she was departing for the realm of the immortals, she must regard mortals as unbearably sullied creatures; why would she consent to linger among them? It is only people's own suspicions that summon evil spirits and malignant influences to plague them.” Though Baochai was speaking to Xiren, her words were really meant for Baoyu to hear. Understanding her intention, Xiren agreed, “There is certainly no such thing. If Miss Lin's spirit were still in the Garden, she thought well enough of us too; how is it that not one of us has ever dreamed of her?” Hearing this from the outer room, Baoyu pondered carefully, “It truly is strange. Ever since I learned that Cousin Lin died, not a day has passed when I have not thought of her several times; yet why have I never dreamed of her? She must have gone up to heaven and, seeing that a common mortal like me cannot commune with the divine, has not appeared even once in my dreams. I shall sleep here in the outer room. Perhaps, since I have returned from the Garden and she knows my devotion is sincere, she will consent to meet me in a dream. I must ask where she has truly gone, so that I may make offerings to her often. But if she truly disdains a sullied creature like me and grants me no dream at all, I shall cease thinking of her.” His mind made up, he said, “I shall sleep in the outer room tonight. None of you need trouble about me.” Baochai did not press him, but merely said, “You must not indulge in wild fancies. Surely you saw how distraught your mother was when you went into the Garden—she was too anxious even to speak. If she learns that you still will not take care of yourself, and the Old Lady should hear of it too, she will say that we have been negligent again.” Baoyu said, “There is no need to say all that. I shall sit here a while and then come in. You are tired too; go to sleep first.” Baochai, believing that he was sure to come in, pretended indifference and said, “I am going to sleep. Let Miss Xiren attend to you.” This suited Baoyu's purpose perfectly. After Baochai had gone to bed, he had Xiren and Sheyue lay out another set of bedding, repeatedly sending someone inside to see whether Second Mistress Bao was asleep. Baochai deliberately feigned sleep, though she herself passed a restless night. When Baoyu believed Baochai asleep, he said to Xiren, “You may all go to bed. I am not grieving. If you do not believe me, help me into bed before you go inside; only take care not to disturb me.” Xiren duly helped him into bed, set tea and water ready, secured the door, and went into the inner room to attend to things there. They all lay down feigning sleep, prepared to come out again if Baoyu stirred.

p.src: When Baoyu saw that Xiren and the others had gone inside, he sent the two old women keeping night watch out of the room. p.src: Baochai rose, washed, and dressed. Accompanied by Ying'er, Xiren, and the others, she first paid her respects to Grandmother Jia, then went to Lady Wang's quarters and made the rounds as far as Xifeng. Returning to Grandmother Jia, she found that her own mother had arrived as well. Everyone asked, “Was Baoyu well last night?” Baochai replied, “He went to sleep as soon as we returned. Nothing was wrong.” Reassured, they went on chatting of other things. Just then a young maid came in and announced, “Second Young Mistress is going home. I heard that someone from Master Sun's household came to the Elder Mistress and said something to her. The Elder Mistress then sent word to Fourth Miss's quarters that there was no need to keep Second Young Mistress here and that she should be allowed to leave. Second Young Mistress is now weeping in the Elder Mistress's quarters. She will probably come here presently to take leave of the Old Lady.” Grandmother Jia and the others were deeply distressed to hear this. They all said, “How could a person like Second Miss be fated to encounter such a man, who will keep her downtrodden all her life? What is to be done?” As they spoke, Yingchun entered, her face stained with tears. Since it was Baochai's happy day, she had no choice but to hold back her tears as she took leave of everyone and prepared to return home. Grandmother Jia knew her suffering and could not very well insist that she stay. She merely said, “You had better go back, then. But do not grieve. Having encountered such a man, there is nothing that can be done. In a few days I shall send someone to fetch you again.” Yingchun said, “You have always loved and cared for me, Old Lady, but now even your love can no longer help me. Alas, I fear I shall never have another chance to come back.” As she spoke, tears streamed down her face. Everyone tried to comfort her: “Why should you be unable to come back? You are not like your Third Sister, who is so far away that it is difficult even to see her.” At the thought of Tanchun, Grandmother Jia and the rest could not keep from shedding tears as well. But because it was Baochai's birthday, they quickly turned sorrow into cheer and said, “That need not be difficult either. The First Lady here is only too eager to see her married and gone.” Aunt Xue said, “I heard today that Miss Shi will soon be going home as well. p.src: Little did they know that the more Baoyu tried to sleep, the wider awake he became. Seeing the two girls laying out their bedding recalled to him the year when Xiren was away from home and Qingwen and Sheyue attended him. One night Sheyue had gone outside, and Qingwen, wishing to frighten her, went after her without putting on enough clothes, caught a chill, and later died from the illness that began then. At this thought, his whole mind turned to Qingwen. Then he suddenly remembered Wang Xifeng saying that Wu'er was the very image of Qingwen, and his yearning for Qingwen shifted to Wu'er. Pretending to be asleep, he stole glances at Wu'er. The longer he looked, the more she resembled Qingwen, and before he knew it his old infatuation had returned. He listened and, hearing no sound from the inner room, knew that those within had fallen asleep. Seeing that Sheyue too was asleep, he deliberately called her name twice, but received no answer. Hearing Baoyu call for someone, Wu'er asked, “What do you require, Second Master?” “I want to rinse my mouth,” Baoyu replied. Seeing that Sheyue was asleep, Wu'er had no choice but to rise. She trimmed the candlewick anew, poured a cup of tea, and brought it over while holding a rinsing bowl in her other hand. Having risen in haste, she wore only a little peach-red satin jacket, and her hair was loosely gathered into a knot. When Baoyu looked at her, it was as though Qingwen had truly come back to life. Suddenly he remembered Qingwen's words: “Had I known I would bear an empty reputation, I might as well have acted upon it in earnest.” He stared at Wu'er in a daze, without even taking the tea.

p.src: Ever since Fangguan had gone away, Wuer had lost all desire to enter the household. Later, when she heard that Xifeng wanted her to come in and attend Baoyu, she became even more eager to do so than Baoyu was to have her. Yet once she had entered, she found Baochai and Xiren alike dignified and composed, and sincerely admired and respected them. She also saw that Baoyu was foolish and distracted, with none of his former charm, and heard that Lady Wang had dismissed all the girls who had joked and played with him. She therefore put the matter out of her mind and no longer harbored the slightest romantic feeling. Unfortunately, that foolish young master mistook her for Qingwen that night and began lavishing tenderness upon her. Wuer’s cheeks had already flushed crimson with embarrassment. Not daring to speak aloud, she could only whisper, “Second Master, rinse your mouth.” Baoyu smilingly took the tea. Whether he rinsed his mouth or not, even he did not know; he merely asked with a grin, “You and Sister Qingwen were close, weren’t you?” Wuer could make neither head nor tail of this and replied, “We were all sisters together. There was no reason for us not to get along.” Baoyu asked softly again, “When Qingwen was gravely ill and I went to see her, didn’t you go too?” Wuer smiled faintly and nodded. Baoyu asked, “Did you hear what she said?” Shaking her head, Wuer replied, “No.” Lost in his memories, Baoyu reached out and caught Wuer by the hand. Wuer flushed in alarm, her heart pounding wildly, and whispered, “Whatever you wish to say, Second Master, please say it. Don’t tug at me like this.” Only then did Baoyu release her hand and say, “She once told me, ‘Had I known I was to bear an empty reputation, I might as well have done what people accused me of.’ How could you not have heard her?” Wuer plainly understood these words as an attempt to take liberties with her, but dared not protest openly. She said, “That was shameless of her. Are such words fit for girls like us to say?” Baoyu cried anxiously, “How is it that you too have become such a moralizing pedant? I only told you this because you look exactly like her. Why must you use such words to insult her?” Wuer still had no idea what Baoyu meant and said, “It is late, Second Master. You should go to sleep. Don’t keep sitting up, or you may catch cold. What did Mistress Baochai and Sister Xiren tell you just now?” “I’m not cold,” said Baoyu. At this point he suddenly noticed that Wuer had no outer garment on. Afraid that she too might catch cold as Qingwen had, he exclaimed, “Why did you come here without putting on something warm?” Wuer replied, “You called so urgently, Master, that there was no time to finish dressing. Had I known we would talk for so long, I would have put it on.”

They opened the door and, finding Baoyu still asleep, wondered, “How is it that he has slept so soundly in the outer room these last two nights?” When Baoyu awoke and saw that everyone else was already up, he hurriedly scrambled to his feet. Rubbing his eyes, he reflected that once again he had not dreamed the previous night: could it be that the paths of immortals and mortals were truly divided? He slowly got out of bed, then remembered Wuer saying the night before that Baochai and Xiren were both like heavenly maidens. There was truth in that, he thought, and he stared blankly at Baochai. Baochai saw him lost in a daze. Though she knew it was on account of Daiyu, she could not tell whether he had dreamed of her or not. His staring made her feel self-conscious, however, so she asked, “Did Second Master really meet an immortal last night?” Hearing this, Baoyu assumed that Baochai had overheard what was said the night before. Forcing a smile, he replied, “Whatever makes you say such a thing?” At this, Wuer felt guiltier than ever. Unable to explain herself, she could only watch Baochai to see how she behaved. Baochai then smiled and asked Wuer, “Did you hear Second Master talking to someone in his sleep?” On hearing this, Baoyu could no longer remain seated and slipped away under the pretense of attending to something else. Wuer's face flushed scarlet, and she could only answer evasively, “He did say a few things during the first half of the night, but I did not hear them clearly. I persuaded Second Master to go to sleep, and afterward I fell asleep too, so I do not know whether he said anything more.” Baochai lowered her head and thought, “Those words were plainly spoken about Daiyu. But if he is continually left to sleep in the outer room, I fear his thoughts may stray and conjure up some flower-spirit or moon-maiden. Besides, his old illness has always sprung from his deep feelings for girls. I must find some way to turn his affections elsewhere; only then can trouble be avoided.” At this thought, her cheeks and ears grew hot. Feeling thoroughly embarrassed, she went into the inner room to wash and dress.

That evening she felt somewhat unwell, and by the next day her chest felt unpleasantly full and tight. Yuanyang and the others wanted to report it to Jia Zheng. But the Lady Dowager forbade them to say anything. “I have been greedy these past two days and eaten a little too much. I shall be well again after going without food for a meal. p.src: That evening Baoyu returned to his own quarters and found that Baochai had only just come back from bidding goodnight to the Lady Dowager and Lady Wang. Remembering what had happened that morning, Baoyu could not help feeling ashamed and remorseful. Seeing him like this, Baochai understood that he felt awkward and reflected, “He is a man ruled by infatuation. If I am to cure this illness of his, I shall have to treat infatuation with infatuation.” After thinking for a while, she asked Baoyu, “Will you be sleeping in the outer room again tonight, then?” Baoyu, conscious of his embarrassment, replied, “The inner room or the outer—it is all the same.” Baochai meant to say more, but found herself too embarrassed. “Oh, enough of this,” said Xiren. “What sense does it make? I refuse to believe you can sleep so soundly out there!” Hearing this, Wuer hastily joined in: “There is nothing else wrong with Second Master sleeping in the outer room, except that he likes to talk in his sleep. No one can make head or tail of it, yet no one dares contradict him either.” Xiren said, “Tonight I shall move out and sleep on that bed myself, and see whether there is any talking in dreams. You need only make up Second Master's bedding in the inner room, and that will settle it.” Baochai heard this but said nothing. Baoyu was already too ashamed to protest, much less argue back, so he consented and moved into the inner room. For his part, Baoyu felt guilty and wished to comfort Baochai; for hers, Baochai feared that brooding might make him ill, and thought it better to show him a little warmth and let him feel some intimacy, thereby substituting one object of affection for another. Thus, that very night, Xiren did indeed move out. With Baoyu remorseful at heart and Baochai intent on winning back his affections, only now, for the first time since their marriage, did they find themselves like fish in water, entwined in tender love—the subtle essences of yin and yang joining and congealing as one, as the saying goes. But that belongs to a later part of the story.

p.src: The next morning, Baoyu and Baochai rose together, and after washing and dressing, Baoyu first went to Grandmother Jia's quarters. Grandmother Jia, who doted on Baoyu and was also mindful of Baochai's filial devotion, suddenly remembered something. She told Yuanyang to open a chest and take out an ancestral Han-dynasty jade pendant. Though it could not compare with Baoyu's own jade, it was still a rare treasure to wear. Yuanyang found it and handed it to Grandmother Jia, saying, “I don't believe I've ever seen this before. Yet after all these years, you remembered so clearly—even which casket in which chest it was kept in—that I found it at once by following your directions. What made you think of taking it out, and what do you intend to do with it?” “You wouldn't know,” replied Grandmother Jia. “This jade was given by my great-grandfather to my grandfather. My grandfather was very fond of me, and just before I married, he summoned me and placed it in my hands himself. He also said, ‘This jade was worn in the Han dynasty and is very precious. Keep it, and whenever you look at it, think of it as seeing me.’ I was still young then, and thought little of it after receiving it, so I tossed it into a chest. After I came here and saw how many fine things our family possessed, this seemed nothing remarkable. I never once wore it, and there it has lain for more than sixty years. Today, seeing how filial Baoyu is, and remembering that he has lost a piece of jade, I thought I would take this out and give it to him, just as my forebear gave it to me.” Presently Baoyu arrived to pay his respects, and Grandmother Jia said delightedly, “Come here. I have something to show you.” Baoyu went to the bedside, and Grandmother Jia handed him the Han jade. Baoyu took it and examined it. It was about three inches across, shaped like a sweet melon, with a reddish blush in its coloring, and exquisitely fashioned. Baoyu praised it again and again. “Do you like it?” asked Grandmother Jia. “My great-grandfather gave it to me. I shall pass it on to you.” Smiling, Baoyu bowed his thanks, then took it away to show his mother. Grandmother Jia said, “If your mother sees it, she'll tell your father, and he'll say once again that I love my grandson more than my son. Neither of them has ever seen it.” Baoyu went off laughing. Baochai and the others spoke with her a little longer, then also took their leave. After this, Grandmother Jia took no food for two days. Her chest remained tight and oppressed, and she suffered from dizziness, blurred vision, and coughing. Ladies Xing and Wang, Xifeng, and the others came to inquire after her. Seeing that Grandmother Jia was still in reasonably good spirits, they merely sent someone to inform Jia Zheng, who came at once to pay his respects. After leaving her room, Jia Zheng immediately sent for a physician to take her pulse. Before long, the physician arrived and examined her pulse. He said that, being advanced in years, she had suffered some indigestion and caught a slight chill, but would recover with a little medicine to aid digestion and dispel the cold. He wrote a prescription. Jia Zheng looked it over, saw that it contained only ordinary medicines, and ordered the servants to prepare the decoction and administer it.

p.src: While Grandmother Jia was ill, the ladies of the entire household came every day without fail to inquire after her health. One day, while they were all there, an old woman who guarded the side gate into the garden came in and reported, “Reverend Miaoyu of Green Bower Hermitage heard that the Old Lady was ill and has come especially to pay her respects.” Everyone said, “She seldom comes over, and today she has made a special visit. Hurry and invite her in.” Xifeng went to Grandmother Jia's bedside and informed her. Xiuyan, being an old acquaintance of Miaoyu's, went out first to welcome her. Miaoyu approached with a maid in attendance, moving with an airy grace. Her hair was arranged in a nun's coil; she wore a plain moon-white silk jacket beneath a long blue-satin patchwork vest with bordered edges, tied with an olive-yellow silk cord, and a white damask skirt painted in pale ink. In her hand she carried a fly whisk and prayer beads. Xiuyan greeted her and said, “When we lived in the garden, I could visit you often. Lately there have been so few people in the garden that it is not easy to venture out alone. Besides, our side gate here is usually locked, so I have not been able to see you these past few days. How fortunate that we meet today.” Miaoyu replied, “Before, you were in the midst of a bustling household. Though you lived in the outer part of the garden, it was still inconvenient for me to visit you often. Now I know that affairs here are not going very well, and I heard that the Old Lady was ill. I was also thinking of you and wanted to see Miss Bao. Why should I care whether your gate is locked? If I wish to come, I shall come; if I do not, even your asking cannot make me.” Xiuyan laughed. “You still have that same temperament.” As they spoke, they reached Grandmother Jia's room. Everyone exchanged greetings with Miaoyu when they saw her. Miaoyu went to Grandmother Jia's bedside, inquired after her health, and offered the customary words of comfort. Grandmother Jia said, “You are a living bodhisattva. Tell me, can my illness be cured or not?” Miaoyu replied, “A benevolent person like you, Old Lady, still has many years allotted to her. This is only a passing cold. A few doses of medicine should soon set you right. At your age, you need only keep your mind at ease.” Grandmother Jia said, “Those things do not trouble me. I am very fond of seeking pleasure. This illness does not feel particularly serious either; it is only that my chest feels tight and unpleasantly full. Just now the physician said it was caused by vexation. You know very well—who would dare vex me? Surely that physician is merely mediocre at reading the pulse. I told Lian that the first physician was right when he diagnosed a cold complicated by indigestion. We shall ask him to come again tomorrow.” Then she told Yuanyang to have the kitchen prepare a table of strictly vegetarian dishes and invited Miaoyu to take a simple meal there. Miaoyu said, “I have already eaten my midday meal. I shall not eat anything.” Lady Wang said, “Then never mind about eating. Stay a little longer, and let us chat.”

Miaoyu replied, “A benevolent person like you, Old Lady, still has many years allotted to her.
This is only a passing cold. A few doses of medicine should soon set you right.
At your age, you need only keep your mind at ease.”

Miaoyu said, “I have already eaten my midday meal. I shall not eat anything.”
Lady Wang said, “Then never mind about eating. Stay a little longer, and let us chat.”

p.src: But contrary to expectation, Grandmother Jia's illness worsened day by day. The physicians' treatments proved ineffective, and later she also developed diarrhea. Jia Zheng grew anxious. Realizing how difficult the illness was to cure, he immediately sent someone to his office to request leave and personally supervised her medicines day and night with Lady Wang. One day, when he saw Grandmother Jia take a little food, his mind was somewhat relieved. Then an old woman was seen peering through the doorway. Lady Wang sent Caiyun to see who it was. Caiyun saw that she was one of the servants who had accompanied Yingchun to the Sun household and asked, “What have you come for?” The old woman replied, “I have been here for ages, but I could not find any of the young ladies. I dared not barge in, yet I am terribly anxious.” Caiyun asked, “What are you anxious about? Has the son-in-law been mistreating our young mistress again?” The old woman said, “The young mistress is gravely ill. There was a quarrel the day before yesterday, and she wept all night. Yesterday phlegm obstructed her breathing. They would not even summon a physician, and today she is worse.” Caiyun said, “The Old Lady is ill. Do not make such a commotion over everything.” Lady Wang had already overheard them from inside. Fearing that the news would distress the Old Lady if she heard it, she hurriedly told Caiyun to take the woman outside to speak. But Grandmother Jia's mind was keen despite her illness, and she happened to hear. “Is Yingchun dying?” she asked. Lady Wang replied, “No. These old women do not know when to hold their tongues. They only said she had been somewhat unwell these past two days and feared she might not recover soon, so they came here to ask for a physician.” Grandmother Jia said, “The physician attending me will do. Send for him at once and have him go.” Lady Wang then had Caiyun tell the old woman to report to the First Lady, and the woman left. Grandmother Jia now grew sorrowful and said, “Of my three granddaughters, one died after enjoying every blessing; the third married far away, so I cannot see her; and though Yingchun has suffered, I thought she might somehow endure it. I never imagined she would die so young. What is the use of letting an old woman like me go on living!” Lady Wang, Yuanyang, and the others spent a long time consoling her. Baochai, Widow Li, and the others were not in the room at the time, while Xifeng had lately been ill. Fearing that sorrow would aggravate Grandmother Jia's illness, Lady Wang sent for them to keep her company. She then returned to her own room, summoned Caiyun, and reproached the old woman for her thoughtlessness. “From now on, when I am with the Old Lady, none of you need come and report matters to me.” The maids obeyed and said nothing. But no sooner had the old woman reached Lady Xing's quarters than someone outside sent word in: “The Second Young Mistress is dead.” When Lady Xing heard the news, she too wept for a while. As Yingchun's father was away from home, she had no choice but to send Jia Lian quickly to see what had happened. Knowing that Grandmother Jia was gravely ill, no one dared report the death to her. Pitiful indeed was this maiden, lovely as a flower and radiant as the moon: married for little more than a year, she was tormented to death by the Sun family.

p.src: The Lady Dowager’s illness worsened day by day, and her thoughts dwelt only on all those dear girls. Presently she thought of Xiangyun and sent someone to see how she was. On returning, the messenger quietly went in search of Yuanyang. As Yuanyang was beside the Lady Dowager, with Lady Wang and the others all present, she could not approach her; so she went to the rear apartments, found Hupo, and told her, “The Lady Dowager was thinking of Miss Shi and sent us to inquire after her. But who could have known that Miss Shi would be weeping inconsolably? She said her husband had been struck by a sudden grave illness. All the physicians had examined him and said he was unlikely to recover; if it turned into consumption, he might still linger for four or five years. That is why Miss Shi is so distressed. She also knows that the Lady Dowager is ill, but she cannot come to pay her respects; she even told me not to mention any of this before the Lady Dowager. If the Lady Dowager should ask, you must find some way to give her another account.” Hupo sighed when she heard this and said nothing. After a long while she said, “You may go.” Hupo could not very well report the truth. She meant to tell Yuanyang and have her invent some story, so she went to the Lady Dowager’s bedside. There she saw that the old lady’s expression had altered drastically, while a roomful of people stood on the floor whispering, “She does not look well.” Hupo dared not speak. Meanwhile Jia Zheng quietly called Jia Lian to his side and whispered a few words in his ear. Jia Lian softly acknowledged his instructions and went out. He assembled all the household servants who were at home and said, “The old lady’s time is nearly upon us. Hurry and send people separately to make the arrangements. First of all, bring out the coffin boards and inspect them, so that the lining may be fitted. Go at once to every quarter, take everyone’s measurements, and write them all down clearly; then have the tailors make the mourning clothes. Settle the arrangements for the funeral awnings, bearers, and ceremonial attendants as well. And several more people should be assigned to the kitchens.” Lai Da and the others replied, “Second Master, you need not trouble yourself over these matters. We made our plans long ago. The only question is, where are we to find the money for it?” Jia Lian said, “There is no need to find money for this. The old lady set it aside herself long ago. Master’s only concern just now was that everything should be properly done, and I think it must also present a respectable appearance to outsiders.” Lai Da and the others assented and sent men off separately to make the preparations.

p.src: Jia Lian returned to his own rooms and asked Ping’er, “How is your mistress today?” Ping’er pursed her lips toward the inner room and said, “Go and see for yourself.” Jia Lian went inside and saw Xifeng trying to dress. Unable to move for the moment, she was leaning against the low table on the kang. Jia Lian said, “I fear you will not be able to stay in bed and nurse yourself much longer. The old lady’s end will come today or tomorrow. How can you possibly keep out of it? Quickly have the rooms put in order; then you must summon your strength and go over there. If anything happens, will you and I be able to come back here?” Xifeng said, “What is there to put in order here? These few things are all we have, so what is there to worry about? You go ahead. Master may be calling for you. I shall come as soon as I have changed my clothes.”

Word came from outside that the Imperial Physician had arrived. Jia Lian ushered him in, and after examining the patient once more, the physician came out and quietly told Jia Lian, “The old lady’s pulse is poor. Be prepared.” Jia Lian understood and informed Lady Wang and the others. Lady Wang at once signaled Yuanyang over with her eyes and told her to prepare the Lady Dowager’s burial clothes. Yuanyang went off to see to it. The Lady Dowager opened her eyes and asked for tea, whereupon Lady Xing offered her a cup of ginseng broth. The Lady Dowager had barely touched it to her lips before saying, “I do not want this. Pour me a cup of tea.” No one dared disobey. Tea was brought at once, and she drank a mouthful. She asked for more, took another sip, and then said, “I want to sit up.” Jia Zheng and the others said, “Whatever you want, old lady, you need only tell us. It would be better not to sit up.” The Lady Dowager said, “That drink of water has made me feel somewhat better. Prop me up a little, so that I may talk with you all.” Zhenzhu and the others gently helped her up with their hands and saw that the Lady Dowager seemed in better spirits now.
